newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn greets EU nod for more Lufthansa share sales.
newsitem.headline: Bonn greets EU nod for more Lufthansa share sales.

text.p: The German transportation ministry welcomed the European Commission's approval for further sales of shares in Lufthansa AG, ministry spokesman Veit Steinle said on Thursday.

The Commission has found a way to ensure that such sales do not discriminate against non-German shareholders, clearing the way for Germany to dispose of more of the 35.7 percent of the airline it still holds.
EU Commissioner Neil Kinnock has sent a letter to German transport minister Matthias Wissmann accepting Wissmann's proposal for a transition period governing such sales, Steinle said in a statement.

Bilateral air traffic agreements between Germany and many other countries stipulate that Lufthansa must remain in the hands of German investors, a condition not easily maintained if the shares are traded freely.
Wissmann's proposal would allow the German government to buy back shares if the German majority in Lufthansa were threatened, Steinle said.
The German government's right to conduct such "last in-first out" purchases would be limited, however.
